symptoms: Diamond-shaped spots on leaves with grey center and brown border. Neck rot causes panicles to break.
cause: Fungal infection favored by high humidity (>90%), moderate temperature (25-28C), and excess nitrogen fertilization.
treatment: Apply Tricyclazole 75WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40EC @ 1.5ml/L. Spray at tillering and panicle initiation stage.
prevention: Use resistant varieties (IR64, Pusa Basmati). Avoid excess nitrogen. Ensure proper spacing for air circulation. Treat seeds with Carbendazim.

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins that turn yellow and then white/grey. Leaves dry from tips downward.
cause: Bacterial infection spread through wind, rain, and contaminated irrigation water. Worsens in rainy season with warm temperatures.
treatment: No effective chemical cure once infected. Remove and destroy infected plants. Apply Streptocycline 0.01% + Copper oxychloride 0.05%.
prevention: Use resistant varieties. Avoid clipping seedling tips during transplanting. Drain excess standing water. Balanced NPK fertilization.

symptoms: Oval/irregular greenish-grey lesions on leaf sheaths near water level. Lesions merge and cause lodging.
cause: Fungus survives in soil. Favored by dense planting, high nitrogen, and warm humid weather (28-32C).
treatment: Spray Validamycin 3L @ 2.5ml/L or Hexaconazole 5EC @ 2ml/L at boot leaf stage.
prevention: Maintain proper spacing. Avoid excess nitrogen. Remove crop residues. Use Trichoderma viride for biocontrol.

symptoms: Orange-brown pustules on leaves (brown rust) or stems (black rust). Yellow rust shows as yellow stripes on leaves.
cause: Fungal spores spread by wind over long distances. Favored by cool nights (10-15C) and warm days (20-25C) with dew.
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25EC @ 1ml/L immediately when pustules appear. Repeat after 15 days if needed.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties (HD-2967, PBW-343). Early sowing (before November 15). Avoid late nitrogen application.

symptoms: Partial conversion of grain into black powder with fishy smell. Only a portion of grains in the ear are affected.
cause: Soil-borne fungus activated by cool temperatures and high humidity during flowering. Rain during heading is critical.
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25EC @ 0.1% at boot leaf and 50% ear emergence stage.
prevention: Seed treatment with Carboxin + Thiram. Avoid irrigation at heading stage if forecast shows rain. Deep summer ploughing.

symptoms: Circular dark brown spots on upper leaf surface. Lower surface shows grey sporulation. Severe defoliation occurs.
cause: Fungal infection favored by warm humid weather (25-30C, >80% RH). Spreads through rain splash.
treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75WP @ 2.5g/L at 30 and 45 days after sowing.
prevention: Crop rotation with cereals. Remove crop debris. Use resistant varieties like GPBD-4, TAG-24.

symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of branches. White fungal mat at stem base. Small round brown sclerotia visible on soil surface.
cause: Soil-borne fungus activated by warm moist conditions. Spreads through contaminated soil and water.
treatment: Apply Carbendazim 50WP @ 1g/L as soil drench around plant base. Repeat after 15 days.
prevention: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed. Deep ploughing in summer. Avoid waterlogging.

symptoms: Water-soaked angular spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halo. Black arm on stems. Boll rot in severe cases.
cause: Bacterial infection spread by rain, wind, and contaminated seed. Warm humid weather (28-33C) favors spread.
treatment: Spray Streptocycline 100ppm + Copper oxychloride 0.3% at first symptom. Repeat every 10 days.
prevention: Acid-delinted seed treatment. Use resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. 3-year crop rotation.

symptoms: Circular holes in bolls with larva feeding inside. Frass visible at entry point. Premature boll opening and shedding.
cause: Moth lays eggs on tender parts. Larvae bore into bolls. Peak activity during flowering (Aug-Oct). Temperature 25-32C ideal.
treatment: Spray Emamectin benzoate 5SG @ 0.2g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5SC @ 0.3ml/L. Apply at ETL of 1 larva per plant.
prevention: Bt cotton varieties. Pheromone traps @ 5/acre. Bird perches @ 20/acre. Neem seed kernel extract 5% as deterrent.

symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring spots on lower leaves first (target-board appearance). Leads to defoliation and fruit rot.
cause: Fungus survives in crop debris. Favored by warm weather (24-29C), high humidity, and stressed plants.
treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75WP @ 2g/L every 10-14 days starting from first symptoms.
prevention: Mulching. Staking to improve air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove lower infected leaves.

symptoms: Upward curling of leaves, thickening, and puckering. Stunted growth. Reduced fruit set. Plants appear bushy.
cause: Virus transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). No cure once infected. Warm dry weather increases whitefly population.
treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy infected plants. Control whitefly with Imidacloprid 17.8SL @ 0.3ml/L.
prevention: Use ToLCV-resistant varieties (Arka Rakshak). Yellow sticky traps for whitefly monitoring. Neem oil 2% spray.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches on leaves and stems. White fungal growth on underside of leaves. Rapid plant death in humid conditions.
cause: Oomycete pathogen favored by cool temperatures (15-22C) and prolonged leaf wetness. Can destroy crop in days.
treatment: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil) @ 2.5g/L immediately. Spray every 5-7 days during active infection.
prevention: Use resistant varieties. Avoid evening irrigation. Ensure proper drainage. Remove volunteer plants.

symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions that enlarge to oval purple spots with concentric rings. Leaves collapse from tip.
cause: Fungal infection favored by warm humid weather (21-30C, >90% RH). Spreads through rain splash and wind.
treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75WP @ 2.5g/L + sticker. Alternate with Tricyclazole. Spray every 10-12 days.
prevention: Proper spacing (15x10cm). Avoid excess irrigation. Raised beds for drainage. Rotate with non-allium crops.

symptoms: Silvery white patches on leaves. Leaves curl and distort. Stunted growth. Bulb size reduction up to 50%.
cause: Tiny sucking insects that rasp leaf surface. Population peaks in hot dry weather (30-35C). Major pest across India.
treatment: Spray Fipronil 5SC @ 1.5ml/L or Spinosad 45SC @ 0.3ml/L. Add sticker for better adhesion on waxy leaves.
prevention: Overhead sprinkler irrigation dislodges thrips. Blue/white sticky traps. Intercrop with coriander as repellent.

symptoms: Dark sunken spots on ripe fruits. Die-back of branches from tip downward. Straw-colored acervuli on lesions.
cause: Seed-borne fungus. Spreads rapidly in warm humid weather (28-32C). Rain splash is primary dispersal method.
treatment: Spray Carbendazim 50WP @ 1g/L + Mancozeb 75WP @ 2.5g/L alternately every 10 days from fruit formation.
prevention: Hot water seed treatment (52C for 30 min). Use certified disease-free seed. Avoid continuous chilli cropping.

symptoms: Upward curling of leaves, bushy appearance, stunted growth. Small leaves with thickened veins. Reduced fruit size.
cause: Transmitted by whiteflies. Similar to tomato leaf curl. Once infected, no cure possible.
treatment: Remove infected plants. Control whitefly vectors with systemic insecticides. Spray Thiamethoxam 25WG @ 0.3g/L.
prevention: Use virus-free nursery. Barrier crops of maize/sorghum. Reflective mulch to repel whiteflies.

symptoms: Reddening of internal cane tissue with white patches. Split cane shows red discoloration. Drying and withering of top.
cause: Fungus enters through borer holes or cut ends. Spreads through contaminated setts and soil. Rainy season peak.
treatment: No effective chemical control. Remove and burn infected canes. Sett treatment with Carbendazim 0.1% for 15-20 minutes.
prevention: Use disease-free setts from healthy crop. Resistant varieties (Co 86032, CoC 671). Hot water treatment of setts (52C, 30 min).

disease: Panama Wilt / Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense)
symptoms: Yellowing of older leaves from margins. Leaf sheaths split longitudinally. Internal pseudostem shows brown/purple discoloration.
cause: Soil-borne fungus that blocks vascular tissue. Spreads through infected suckers and contaminated soil. No cure once in soil.
treatment: No effective chemical treatment. Inject Carbendazim 50WP at stem base of healthy plants as preventive.
prevention: Use tissue-culture plants. Avoid planting in previously infected fields for 5 years. Resistant varieties (FHIA-01).

symptoms: Yellow streaks on leaves that enlarge to oval brown spots with grey center. Severe cases cause premature leaf death.
cause: Fungal airborne spores. Warm humid conditions (25-28C, >90% RH). Windward side of plants affected first.
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25EC @ 1ml/L or Mancozeb 75WP @ 2.5g/L. Alternate fungicides to prevent resistance.
prevention: Remove infected leaves. Ensure proper drainage and spacing. Avoid overhead irrigation.

symptoms: Ragged holes in leaves with large amounts of frass. Larvae hide in whorl. Can destroy young crop completely.
cause: Invasive pest (arrived India 2018). Moths migrate long distances. Multiple generations per year. Active at night.
treatment: Spray Emamectin benzoate 5SG @ 0.4g/L in whorl. Chlorantraniliprole 18.5SC @ 0.4ml/L. Apply with high volume.
prevention: Early sowing. Pheromone traps for monitoring. Sand + lime powder application in whorl. Release Trichogramma parasitoid.

symptoms: Bright yellow mosaic pattern on leaves. Leaves become small and distorted. Pod formation severely reduced.
cause: Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). No cure. Warm weather (28-35C) increases vector activity.
treatment: No chemical cure. Remove infected plants. Control whitefly with Thiamethoxam 25WG @ 0.3g/L.
prevention: Use resistant varieties (JS 335, JS 97-52). Early sowing to escape peak whitefly season. Border crop of maize.

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on rhizome. Yellowing and wilting of pseudostem from base upward. Foul smell from rotting rhizome.
cause: Soil-borne oomycete. Waterlogging and poor drainage trigger infection. High soil moisture and warm temperature.
treatment: Drench with Metalaxyl (Ridomil) 2g/L around plant base. Remove and destroy infected plants. Improve drainage.
prevention: Seed rhizome treatment with Mancozeb 0.3% for 30 min. Raised beds. Trichoderma harzianum application @ 5kg/acre.

symptoms: White blister-like pustules on lower leaf surface. Malformation of flowers (stag-head symptom). Stunted pods.
cause: Oomycete pathogen favored by cool humid weather (10-20C, >70% RH). Peak in December-January in North India.
treatment: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil MZ) 2.5g/L at onset. Repeat after 15 days.
prevention: Resistant varieties. Timely sowing (October). Removal of infected plant parts. Avoid excess nitrogen.

symptoms: Drooping of petioles and leaflets without yellowing. Plants dry while maintaining green color (sudden wilt). Root shows dark discoloration.
cause: Soil-borne fungus. Can persist in soil for 6+ years. Warm temperature (25-30C) and moderate soil moisture trigger disease.
treatment: No effective field control. Seed treatment with Carbendazim + Thiram (1:1) @ 3g/kg seed.
prevention: Resistant varieties (JG-62, Avrodhi). 4-5 year crop rotation with cereals. Trichoderma viride @ 2.5kg mixed with FYM.

symptoms: Chlorotic streaks on leaves. White cottony growth on lower leaf surface. Ear malformation (green ear disease).
cause: Oomycete spread through soil-borne oospores and airborne sporangia. Cool nights with dew favor infection.
treatment: Spray Metalaxyl 35SD @ 2g/kg seed as treatment. Remove and destroy infected plants showing green ear.
prevention: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl. Resistant hybrids (ICTP 8203). Avoid ratooning from infected fields.

symptoms: Older leaves turn uniformly pale yellow-green. Stunted growth. Reduced tillering in cereals. Early maturity with low yield.
cause: Low soil nitrogen, heavy rains leaching nitrogen, sandy soils with poor retention, or insufficient fertilization.
treatment: Apply urea @ 25-50 kg/acre as top dressing. Foliar spray of 2% urea solution for quick correction.
prevention: Split nitrogen application in 3 doses. Green manuring with dhaincha/sunnhemp. Use neem-coated urea for slow release.

symptoms: Dark green leaves with purple/reddish discoloration on lower leaves. Delayed maturity. Poor root development.
cause: Low available phosphorus in soil (common in acidic and alkaline soils). Fixation in iron/aluminum-rich soils.
treatment: Apply Single Super Phosphate @ 50kg/acre or DAP @ 25kg/acre. Rock phosphite for acidic soils.
prevention: Apply phosphorus at sowing time near root zone. Use PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria) biofertilizer.

symptoms: Marginal leaf scorch (browning of leaf edges) starting from older leaves. Weak stems prone to lodging. Small, shriveled grains.
cause: Light-textured soils with low K reserves. Intensive cropping without K fertilization. Heavy leaching in sandy soils.
treatment: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) @ 25-40 kg/acre. Foliar spray of 1% KCl solution for quick response.
prevention: Regular soil testing. Include K in fertilizer schedule. Crop residue incorporation recycles K.

symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young leaves (veins remain green, tissue turns yellow). Severe cases show white leaves. Common in calcareous soils.
cause: High soil pH (>7.5) makes iron unavailable. Waterlogging. Excess phosphorus or zinc in soil.
treatment: Foliar spray of Ferrous sulfate 0.5% + citric acid 0.1%. Soil application of FeSO4 @ 10kg/acre with organic matter.
prevention: Maintain soil pH below 7.5. Apply organic matter. Use iron-efficient crop varieties.
